reference: Installed zstdcat CLI (the zstd package alias), independently constructed small Zstandard frames; no candidate-generated oracle bytes. Bash metadata is a separate contract.
coverage: Named-file decode preserves exact binary output including NUL and 0xff bytes.
Explicit '-' input reads compressed bytes from standard input.
Concatenated unknown-content-size frames decode in order.
Multiple named inputs concatenate without inserted separators.
A valid empty frame produces empty output.
-- permits a filename beginning with a dash.
Ordinary noncompressed input passes through; recognized incomplete frames fail.
Processing continues across raw and encoded operands in order.
The reference no-operand stdin behavior is compared with the loadable behavior.
Bash builtin type/help metadata matches the documented name and purpose.
Default stdin passes plain binary bytes through; embedded magic after a raw prefix is copied without scanning.
Each short ordinary operand and each 1–3 byte partial magic is independent raw input, matching the reference; a full four-byte magic is recognized and tested separately.
A finite producer splits the four-byte magic across delayed writes; decoder selection must wait for enough bytes and produce the complete decoded payload.
Recheck format at complete frame boundaries, even when the following raw prefix arrives in separate short pipe writes.

Complete standard and skippable magic bytes select strict decoding, even with force pass-through enabled. Incomplete bodies, next-frame headers and skippable payloads fail; later operands are still processed.
Supported skippable and complete empty frames produce no raw bytes and can precede a normal frame.
exclusions: A decoder frame advertising a window above the documented 128 MiB limit is deferred because exercising it may allocate more than 128 MiB; the required future VM and independent fixture are specified below.
No compression behavior is tested because zstdcat is a decompressor-only loadable.
Broken-output-pipe and injected I/O failure behavior are outside these bounded byte-parity fixtures.
Other compression formats, legacy Zstandard frame versions, dictionaries and undocumented options are outside the supported decoder subset. Full zstd CLI conformance is not claimed.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Decode an independently encoded raw-block frame from a named file and preserve all output bytes, including NUL and 0xff; tree comparison also checks that zstdcat leaves its input in place.
Verify the documented '-' operand reads a compressed stream from standard input and writes only decoded bytes to stdout.
Decode two concatenated non-single-segment frames with unknown content sizes, in order and without frame separators.
Verify successive named files are decoded to one stdout stream with no inserted delimiter.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x04\x21\x00\x00one\n' > first.zst
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x04\x21\x00\x00two\n' > second.zst
zstdcat first.zst second.zst

cases.purpose: Decode a valid empty Zstandard frame and distinguish it from an empty or malformed compressed input.
Verify '--' ends option parsing so a relative compressed filename beginning with '-' is treated as an input operand.
Check Installed zstdcat pass-through behavior for a non-Zstandard file: its bytes are emitted unchanged with success, rather than a decoder error.
cases.script:
printf 'not a zstd frame\n' > bad.zst
zstdcat bad.zst

cases.purpose: Check failure on a frame header that advertises six content bytes but ends before its block header.
Pass an ordinary raw operand between complete encoded operands, preserve byte order, and return success.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x07\x39\x00\x00before\n' > before.zst
printf 'bad' > broken.zst
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00after\n' > after.zst
zstdcat before.zst broken.zst after.zst

cases.purpose: Empty default stdin is attempted as encoded input and fails with status 1, rather than a usage error.
Use Bash metadata builtins to verify zstdcat is registered as a builtin and its help includes the documented function and exit status.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t zstdcat)
doc=$(help zstdcat)
[[ $kind == builtin ]]
[[ $doc == *'Decompress zstd files to standard output.'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'Exit status: 0, or 1 if any file failed.'* ]]
printf 'builtin help contract ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented decoder window ceiling using a small frame that advertises a window above 128 MiB.
Default stdin passes plain binary bytes through; embedded magic after a raw prefix is copied without scanning.
Each short ordinary operand and each 1–3 byte partial magic is independent raw input, matching the reference; a full four-byte magic is recognized and tested separately.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x61' > plain1
printf '%b' '\x28' > prefix1
printf '%b' '\x61\x62' > plain2
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5' > prefix2
printf '%b' '\x61\x62\x63' > plain3
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f' > prefix3
zstdcat plain1 prefix1 plain2 prefix2 plain3 prefix3

cases.purpose: A finite producer splits the four-byte magic across delayed writes; decoder selection must wait for enough bytes and produce the complete decoded payload.
Recheck format at complete frame boundaries, even when the following raw prefix arrives in separate short pipe writes.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > frame
{ cat frame; printf x; /usr/bin/sleep 0.02; printf '%b' '\x00tail\xff'; } | zstdcat -

cases.purpose: Complete standard and skippable magic bytes select strict decoding, even with force pass-through enabled. Incomplete bodies, next-frame headers and skippable payloads fail; later operands are still processed.
cases.script:
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd' > magic
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61' > body
printf '%b' '\x50\x2a\x4d\x18\x02\x00\x00\x00' > skip
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd' > joined
printf '%b' '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x06\x31\x00\x00\x41\x6c\x70\x68\x61\x0a' > good
zstdcat magic body skip joined good

cases.purpose: Supported skippable and complete empty frames produce no raw bytes and can precede a normal frame.
